solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criminal act, one perpetrated in prison?

definitions.meaning: a crime committed by or with help from someone within the organisation robbed
whimsically, a job done by a prisoner who is literally inside, slang for in jail

explanation.surface: A question about a crime carried out by someone already behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' is everyday slang for in prison, which gives the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside job is a crime done with help from an insider, such as an employee.

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a sect is a group that has broken away from a larger church

explanation.surface: A bug spreading among a well-liked protest faction.
explanation.definitionFit: Bug is an everyday word for an insect or creepy-crawly.

definitions.meaning: a ... pigeon is a decoy or police informer

explanation.surface: Someone asking which seat suits a pigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool is a simple seat, and 'stool pigeon' is the idiom for an informer or decoy bird.

clue.text: Man wrestling with deity is explosive

indicators.note: wrestling suggests the two words grappling and getting their letters tangled together

explanation.surface: A mortal grappling with a god makes for a volatile contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrestling with' mixes the letters of MAN and DEITY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamite is a blasting substance, a classic example of a high explosive.

clue.text: Contemplate but don't act; that shouldn't happen

definitions.meaning: to merely think of something rather than doing it
the exclamation '...!' expresses dismay at an outrageous idea

explanation.surface: Advice to ponder without doing, and a protest that something must not occur.
explanation.definitionFit: Read flatly the phrase means only imagine it; as an exclamation it voices shocked disapproval.

parts.note: rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A card game featured in a UK paper's puzzle pages.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAG is an old British card game, a forerunner of poker.
explanation.definitionFit: Brag is a traditional gambling game played with cards, similar to poker.

indicators.note: rejected suggests something sent back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to dub someone is to give them a name

explanation.surface: An American pal's name has been turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Bud is US slang for a buddy or mate.

clue.text: Courage of supporter to a great degree

parts.note: a bra is a garment that supports, a crossword favourite
very means extremely or to a great degree

explanation.surface: A fan who is enormously brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravery and courage are synonyms for the quality of facing danger without fear.

clue.text: Extremely dire, lengthy journey, not a direct route

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, so only its two ends are kept

parts.note: a tour is an extended trip

explanation.surface: A grim, long trip that wanders off the straight path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'dire' but takes its end letters, DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A detour is a roundabout way taken instead of the direct road.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A farmer sneering at a meagre harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorn someone is to despise them or treat them with disdain.

clue.text: Perhaps tape large creature next to tiny one

parts.note: a seal is a big marine mammal
an ant is a tiny creature

explanation.surface: Setting a big animal beside a minuscule one, with tape somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks tape as just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tape can be used to seal gaps, so it is one example of a sealing material.

definitions.meaning: ... Jane is the title character of the 1953 film musical starring Doris Day

explanation.surface: A judgement that a singer called Jane was a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: Calamity Jane was a real Wild West figure, best known from the Doris Day musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamity means a great misfortune, and it is also the nickname completing Jane in the musical's title.

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per person'

explanation.surface: Allocating a plot of land to every university.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a country in South America, and land here means a nation.

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A great Renaissance genius whose life was never thrown off course by hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' shuffles the letters of NO ORDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was a painter, inventor and scientist, the archetypal Renaissance man of many talents.

definitions.meaning: '...!' is an emphatic British way of saying no way

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing a request as unlikely and flatly saying no.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means unlikely, and as an exclamation it is a firm refusal.

clue.text: Unforced, one may cancel a flat

definitions.meaning: in music a ... sign cancels a preceding flat or sharp

explanation.surface: Something effortless, and something that may annul a flat, like an apartment lease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but is the musical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural means relaxed and unaffected; in notation the natural sign restores a note lowered by a flat.

parts.note: a whack is an informal word for a portion, as in 'pay your whack'
O resembles zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: Sharing nothing with others is called crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Whacko is informal for crazy or eccentric.

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters here

parts.note: flex is the British word for an electric cable on an appliance

explanation.surface: A twitch caused by a partly understood wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps RE from 'read'; FLEX is British for an appliance's power lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex is an automatic bodily reaction, such as a knee jerk.

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
ate means consumed or swallowed

explanation.surface: Henry gulped down a powerful feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed' looks like a containment signal but is simply ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate is intense dislike, a powerful feeling.

clue.text: Horribly sick near use of cosmetics

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are badly mangled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeling queasy close to someone applying makeup.
explanation.definitionFit: Skincare is the routine of applying creams and lotions to look after the complexion.

indicators.note: first off says the opening letter is removed from the word

parts.note: daunts means disheartens or discourages

explanation.surface: Before anything, someone puts off their kin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First off' looks like 'to begin with' but drops the D of DAUNTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunts are family members, sisters of a parent.

indicators.note: fails suggests the word breaks down, so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An upmarket store goes bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh means stylish, upper-class or elegant.

clue.text: Vehicle snooty type gets to take away

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
toff is British slang for an upper-class, stuck-up person

explanation.surface: A posh person gets the car to drive off with.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a well-to-do snob.
explanation.definitionFit: To cart something off is to remove it, often forcibly.

clue.text: Some children always concerned with part of body

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some children always have an interest in anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal means relating to the kidneys, which are organs of the body.

clue.text: Solemn person starts to offer wise lessons

indicators.note: starts are the opening letters, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A serious figure begins to give sage teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the first letters of offer, wise and lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: An owl stands for a grave, wise-looking person, from the bird's serious appearance.

clue.text: Taken by surprise being put out of cricket ground?

definitions.meaning: to be stunned or knocked off balance
in cricket a ball hit over the boundary without bouncing scores six runs

explanation.surface: Someone startled at being thrown out of a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, hitting the ball clean over the boundary scores six; 'put out' plays on cricket's sense of dismissing a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means shocked or overwhelmed, borrowed from the cricket shot that sends the ball out of the field.
